voice: a developer on the team who owns the reporting API, writing to a teammate
brief: Phase: long multi-phase, idea to ship. Role: developer. Repo: a Node.js reporting API (accounts, invoices, line items) on node:http, with a repository layer over JSON-lines data files, a small job runner, a per-account concurrency guard, config/limits.json, a flag registry and metrics catalogue in ops/, and docs for a partner that imports exports. The ask: a customer can download all their invoices as a CSV file, including accounts with a few hundred thousand rows, without the service running out of memory, with the same columns the partner already imports. Traps to plant (adapt, five or more): (1) the existing list endpoint loads every row into memory, and the repository has a streaming reader nobody uses; (2) text fields can start with = + - or @ and spreadsheet programs run them as formulas, so the export must neutralise them, but docs/partners.md says the partner parses negative amounts, so numeric columns must not be altered; (3) docs/partners.md fixes the column order, a header spelling and ISO dates in UTC, and the existing JSON endpoint formats dates in local time; (4) the per-account concurrency guard allows one running job and the runner has no cancel on client disconnect; (5) the metrics catalogue has only some names (export_started, export_failed, export_duration_ms), and the rollout must gate on those and on the rings in ops/. Decisions the design note must settle: streaming versus a prepared file, formula neutralisation, limits, cancel, rollout order. The feature is built end to end: the request asks for a short design note, the feature with tests, a rollout plan and a release note.
